circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has served as the venue for Formula One's season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. The circuit represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One venues, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Melbourne's Albert Park Circuit winds around a lakeside park in the city's Albert Park suburb and hosts the Australian Grand Prix each year alongside supporting racing series. The track holds FIA Grade 1 status, qualifying it for top-tier international motorsport competition.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: The Red Bull Ring, situated in Spielberg, Austria, is a 4. 326 km motorsport facility that hosted the Austrian Grand Prix during two separate periods: initially as the Österreichring from 1970 to 1987, and later as the A1-Ring following its reconstruction and modification from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street course in Azerbaijan positioned along Baku Boulevard, spanning 6. 003 km per lap and ranking as the fourth-longest track in Formula One. The venue hosted its first F1 race as the 2016 European Grand Prix, before becoming a permanent fixture on the calendar as the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km facility that hosted the first Formula One grand prix ever held in the Middle East and continues to annually stage the Bahrain Grand Prix alongside other racing series. The FIA Grade 1-licensed track has accommodated various motorsport events including drag racing, GP2, and endurance competitions, while featuring multiple configurable layouts.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located near Barcelona in Montmeló, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations that make it suitable for testing all aspects of vehicle performance. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The 7. 004 km circuit at Francorchamps in Belgium has been hosting the Belgian Grand Prix since 1925, appearing on the inaugural Formula One calendar in 1950. The venue has maintained annual Grand Prix races from 1985 onwards, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, this 4. 361 km track serves as the home of Formula One's Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond its F1 duties, the circuit has accommodated various international motorsport competitions, including world sportscar championships and multiple North American racing series.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit, located in Shanghai's Jiading District, hosted the Chinese Grand Prix annually from 2004 until 2019 before resuming in 2024. The venue also began hosting the Shanghai ePrix electric racing championship in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, England, this renowned racing facility has been the traditional home of the British Grand Prix since 1948 and hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After rotating between three venues for three decades, the Grand Prix has been permanently held at this circuit since 1987, which also serves as the British stop on the MotoGP calendar.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest became the first Formula One venue in Eastern Europe when it hosted its inaugural grand prix in 1986, constructed in just eight months, faster than any other Formula One circuit. Located outside the Hungarian capital near a major highway, the 4. 381 km track was built as a compromise after plans for a street circuit in Budapest's largest park were rejected by the government.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km Italian racing circuit built in 1922 near Milan, making it mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built track and home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949 (except during 1980 renovations). Renowned as "the Temple of Speed" for its characteristic long straights and fast-flowing corners, the venue has become synonymous with high-speed racing.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km motorsport venue in Mie Prefecture, Japan, operated by Honda Mobilityland with a spectator capacity of 155,000. The track is renowned for hosting rounds of the Formula One World Championship and the Japanese Super Formula series.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running adjacent to Las Vegas proper and featuring the famous Las Vegas Boulevard lined with major hotels and casinos. The track incorporates several iconic landmarks such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as it winds through the urban landscape.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez in Mexico City is a 4. 304 km circuit named after two fatal racing drivers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who died in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The venue has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix across three separate eras, with the modern incarnation resuming in 2015 on its current configuration after a 23-year absence, now officially branded as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary racing facility constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and a qualifying average speed near 139 mph. Designed by specialist F1 circuit architects, it was purpose-built to host the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the championship calendar beginning in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a compact 3. 337 km street circuit winding through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, following the harbour's perimeter in the Principality of Monaco. Though officially named after Monaco itself, the circuit is commonly known as Monte Carlo, reflecting its location predominantly within that particular district.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, the 4. 259 km Zandvoort circuit hosted the Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until its final scheduled race in 2026. The seaside venue, situated 35 km west of Amsterdam, marked Formula One's return to the Netherlands after a lengthy absence.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Located north of Doha in Qatar, the Lusail International Circuit stretches 5. 419 kilometres and features a 1. 068-kilometre main straight, holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing circuit in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate late Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who tragically died in an aviation accident. The counterclockwise track hosts major international motorsport events and features additional facilities including a karting venue dedicated to another notable Brazilian racing driver.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street-based racing venue situated along the Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, which has been home to the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural running in 2021. The facility also began hosting Formula E racing in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a temporary track that winds through Singapore's Marina Bay area, incorporating sections of the Downtown Core and Kallang districts into its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish racing venue is renowned as a versatile circuit that tests multiple driver skills through its combination of extended straightaways and diverse corner configurations. The facility holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 FIA facility that regularly hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside major racing events including MotoGP and the FIA World Endurance Championship. The track has previously accommodated various motorsport series ranging from IndyCar to sports car championships and rallycross competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Thai and British driver Alexander Albon currently races for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai national flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, bringing two world championship titles from his 2005-2006 stint with Renault and 32 career Grand Prix victories across two decades. Beyond his single-seater success, Alonso has distinguished himself in endurance racing by winning the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship and twice capturing the 24 Hours of Le Mans, making him the sole driver to claim both Formula One and world sportscar championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli joined Mercedes in 2025 and has already secured six Formula One victories during his debut season.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor currently racing for Haas in Formula One.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabi Bortoleto, a Brazilian motorsport competitor, currently races in Formula One representing Audi in the championship.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from over a decade of competition in the sport. He achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his tenure with Mercedes, while accumulating 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Argentine driver Franco Alejandro Colapinto currently races in Formula One for the Alpine team. He has established himself as a competitor in the sport's top category.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, currently holds a reserve role with Haas in Formula One while competing in European Le Mans Series prototypes with Nielsen Racing. He made seven Formula One race appearances during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix at Monza marked his sole victory to date, achieved during his time with AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver competing in Formula One for Red Bull Racing under French nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has claimed seven World Drivers' Championship titles, equalling Michael Schumacher's record. The accomplished competitor also holds multiple circuit records, including the most career victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One while maintaining an impressive endurance racing résumé that includes a 2015 Le Mans 24 Hours victory with Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor currently driving for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver competing for Ferrari, finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship and has claimed nine race victories throughout his Formula One career spanning nine seasons.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen, known as K-Mag, returned to Formula One for the 2022 season after a two-year absence, competing through 2024 before focusing on other racing commitments. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship with BMW through WRT and competes part-time in NASCAR's Cup Series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship with the team. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 12 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French driver, currently races for Haas in Formula One. He previously achieved a notable career milestone by securing victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Checo Pérez is a Mexican driver currently competing in Formula One for Cadillac. The experienced racer finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while at Red Bull and has accumulated six race victories throughout his 15-year career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri competes for McLaren in Formula One, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories since joining the grid four seasons ago.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by his "Honey Badger" moniker, competed in Formula One throughout a 14-season span from 2011 until 2024, securing victories in eight Grand Prix events during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has accumulated seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-year career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American racing driver who currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition. After competing in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons, he has transitioned to sports car racing, having previously driven in IMSA's LMP2 class for Era Motorsport.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian formula one driver currently racing for Aston Martin in the sport's top championship series.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver currently fulfilling a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls after competing in the sport's top category between 2021 and 2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Max Verstappen is a Dutch racing driver competing for Red Bull Racing who has secured four consecutive Formula One World Drivers' Championship titles between 2021 and 2024. With 71 Grand Prix victories accumulated across 12 seasons, he stands as one of the sport's most successful drivers.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China as a Formula One driver, currently functioning as a reserve driver for Cadillac after competing in the championship between 2022 and 2024. He holds the distinction of being the sole Chinese national to have raced in Formula One.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine since 2021, inheriting Renault's works operation after a rebrand designed to showcase the French manufacturer's sports car division. Operating with a Mercedes power unit and French racing licence, Alpine achieved its only victory under this identity when Esteban Ocon triumphed at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, before Renault's departure from the sport concluded the team's tenure as a manufacturer-backed operation at the end of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British manufacturer, has competed in Formula One across multiple iterations, with its current competitive entry operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of Italian automaker Ferrari, stands as Formula One's most enduring and accomplished team, competing continuously since the championship's inception in 1950. The squad's iconic "Prancing Horse" emblem has become synonymous with the sport's prestige and tradition.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed F1 team in 2014, with operations commencing in the 2016 season. Ayao Komatsu took over as team principal in 2024, succeeding Guenther Steiner who led the outfit since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering firm established itself through endurance racing success including the 1989 Le Mans victory before joining Formula One in 1993. The team competed as an independent constructor for over three decades, becoming the fourth-longest-serving chassis manufacturer in the sport's history before ceasing operations in 2025, when Audi acquired its assets to establish its own F1 program.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited represents Britain's presence in Formula One through its Woking-based operation, functioning as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under Mumtalakat Holding Company's ownership.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with the current team operating from Brackley under a German licence. The outfit, officially Mercedes-AMG Petronas, saw ownership restructured in 2022 when Ineos joined as an equal partner alongside the Mercedes-Benz Group and team principal Toto Wolff. The marque's racing efforts are traditionally associated with the "Silver Arrows" designation.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024, owned by Red Bull GmbH alongside Red Bull Racing. Operating from Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the team functions as the second constructor within the Red Bull organizational structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that debuted in 2024 as one of two Red Bull-owned squads alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with operations near Milton Keynes, the team operates as part of the Red Bull GmbH motorsport portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team established in 2005 and headquartered in England, owned by the Red Bull GmbH conglomerate. Under Christian Horner's leadership from its inception through 2024, the team established itself as a major competitive force in the sport before Horner's departure and replacement by Laurent Mekies. Red Bull GmbH operates a second Formula One team, Racing Bulls, alongside its main racing operation.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, a British constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, represents one of Formula One's most storied operations. Competing as Atlassian Williams F1 Team from 2026, the team emerged following Williams's prior unsuccessful venture and operates from its base in Grove, Oxfordshire.
